mainEntity.name: How Many Templates Should an Agency Keep?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four or five. Enough to cover the client types you win, few enough that everyone on the team knows each one well. Past that, the time you save on layout gets spent choosing.

mainEntity.name: Can You Save Your Own Templates in Sitejet?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. From the website list, open Actions and choose Create as template. It's stored under My templates and can be shared to other accounts with a code from Copy & Share Websites.

mainEntity.name: Should a Template Include Real Content?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Use placeholder copy, neutral images and bracketed fields for names, addresses and legal details, because real content from one client has a way of surviving into the next client's site.

mainEntity.name: Do Templates Make Every Site Look the Same?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you template the design instead of the setup. Standardise the sections, the settings and the checklist. Change the colours, type and imagery every time.

mainEntity.name: How Long Does It Take to Build a Template Library?

acceptedAnswer.text: One good project per template, plus an hour to strip and save it. Most agencies already have five suitable projects in the archive. The work is picking which five.

HowTo.name: How to create and share your own template in Sitejet
HowTo.description: Turn a signed-off client site into a reusable template and share it with your team.

step.name: Wait for written sign-off
step.text: Save a template only after the client has approved the site and launch QA is done, so the template carries the fixes as well as the layout.

step.name: Strip the client's content
step.text: Swap their copy for placeholder text, their images for neutral ones, and their details for bracketed fields such as [CLIENT NAME].

step.name: Create the template
step.text: Open the Actions menu on the website and choose Create as template. It appears under Templates in the top menu bar, in My templates.

step.name: Share it with the team
step.text: From the burger menu, open Copy & Share Websites and generate a Perpetual code for a template you will hand out more than once, or a One-time code for a single copy.
